issue.title: test_expanded_overflowing_header_claims_half_page_scroll fails: deck pin settles at 2.0 after the sync read
issue.description:
`tests/ace/tui/widgets/test_agent_header_panel.py::test_expanded_overflowing_header_claims_half_page_scroll`
fails deterministically: `assert 2.0 == 0.0` at test_agent_header_panel.py:703.

sase-1ab.4 note #4 diagnosed it: `pin_to_bottom` applies asynchronously while the test
reads the deck scroll offset synchronously, and the pinned deck then follows to 2.0. The
deck/pin machinery dates from the sase-19x card-block work. Decide whether the test
should wait for the pin to settle or whether the header's half-page scroll claim is
genuinely wrong, then fix the test or the behavior.

Reported independently by sase-1ab.2 note #3, sase-1ab.4 note #4, and sase-1ab.7 note #2
(all on clean base trees). Reproduced again by the sase-1ab land agent at sase master
7b20f4c1c in the full fast suite and in a serial rerun. Not caused by the turn rename.

task_type_fields.why_not_flake: Fails the same way (assert 2.0 == 0.0) in the parallel full suite, a serial rerun, and three earlier clean-base runs by separate agents.

issue.creation_reason: Three turn-rename phases (sase-1ab.2, .4, .7) independently reported this clean-base failure and no bead tracks it; the sase-1ab land agent reproduced it at master.

evidence.note: sase-1b1 land agent: fails deterministically (assert 2.0 == 0.0 at test_agent_header_panel.py:703, main-scroll scroll_y 2) on master 372ecc97c3 in the escalated full lane (tool run 81ef0cb11e86e4cdaaa8b70cfeb11615) and in a focused serial rerun. It fails the same way on a pre-deck-views worktree (9c4d104aff~1), so the deck-views badge and view-policy work did not cause it. sase-1b1.4 note #4 recorded the same pre-existing failure.
